title: Solar Si appendix

products.stat_basis: quantiser-floor 0.01 dex (RYA-771) — UNMEASURED: line-to-line scatter at n_lines=1; the floor STANDS IN for a scatter that was never determined, it is not a measurement of one

components.name: measurement
components.source: Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1: one line -> statistical error from the goodness of the profile fit; chi2-curvature sigma of this line, rescaled to red_chi2 = 1

evidence.likelihood: synthesis chi2 over the fit window, curvature at the best abundance
evidence.correlation_treatment: red_chi2 rescaling absorbs pixel correlation and model inadequacy; the worse-constrained side is taken

components.name: transition_data
components.source: gf covariance per data/reference/gf_error_model.csv -- AGSS21_Si_Amarsi2017: scale_only (scale 0.0189 dex; Pehlivan Rhodin+2024 Table B.2 (OL91 lifetimes); Amarsi & Asplund 2017 Sect. 1)

components.name: stellar.logg
components.source: solar log g is pinned; delta_logg is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.metallicity
components.source: solar [Fe/H] is pinned; delta_feh is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.teff
components.source: sourced DEFINED zero (RYA-1226 convention): the solar Teff allowance is 1 K

evidence.owed_measurement: a Teff perturbation on this pool

components.name: model_atmosphere
components.source: Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1: half the mean (<3D> - Holweger & Mueller 1974) (+) half the mean (3D - <3D>), per-line LTE abundances of Scott+2015 I/II (pool lines, n=1)

components.name: blends
components.source: full atomic + molecular synthesis in-window (RYA-1230 turned molecular opacity on in every band); no catalogued-blend deficit

body_html:
Solar silicon: 7.573 ± 0.036

Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse 2021: 7.51 ± 0.03  ·  this measurement +0.063 dex

Measured the way Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse (2021) measure it: the Asplund et al. 2021 line set (Amarsi & Asplund 2017: nine Si I and one Si II line), 10 lines measured on one spectrum, each part weighted by its uncertainty.

  • Si I: 7.580 ± 0.037 · Kitt Peak (1984, molecfit) · VIS · Si I · Asplund et al. 2021 lines · 3D NLTE (Amarsi)
  • Si II: 7.522 ± 0.038 · Kitt Peak (1984, molecfit) · VIS · Si II · Asplund et al. 2021 lines · 1D LTE
  • Si I: 7.650 ± 0.051 · Kitt Peak (1984, molecfit) · red-optical · Si I · Asplund et al. 2021 lines · 3D NLTE (Amarsi)

Line grades

Every product is measured on one of three grades of spectral lines and the grades are never mixed in one number.

Line grades
GradeWhat it meansThis element

How to read this forest. Each row is one independent product, preserving its band, holding, engine, indicator and line set. Engines and indicator families are never averaged. Each bar is the uncertainty as Asplund et al. 2021 quote it: line-to-line scatter, the 3D-model term and the NLTE term (at least 0.03 dex). For a molecule the NLTE term is replaced by its dependence on the other element, and the 3D term comes from the 3D-to-1D difference Amarsi et al. 2021 publish for the same band. Atomic-data and observational terms are not in the bar, as in Asplund; they stay in the full error budget attached to the row. Grades describe the supplied line-pool provenance, not engine quality; evaluated theoretical CNO oscillator strengths are not relabelled as laboratory evidence. Quarantined, failed and unconstrained fits have no abundance mark. Experimental products remain explicitly not adopted. Literature references provide context, never tuning targets.

How this was measured

Every silicon value on this page comes from fitting synthetic spectra to the observed solar spectrum, line by line or band by band, with the silicon abundance as the free parameter. The synthesis includes the atomic lines and the molecular opacity in every window, so blended absorption is modelled rather than attributed to the line being measured. The continuum is placed locally around every line by comparing the observation with the synthesis on its own highest pixels, and ground-based spectra are telluric-corrected across their full range.

Each indicator is measured independently on each solar spectrum and reported separately; nothing is averaged across indicators or instruments. Where a 3D or NLTE correction is published for the lines, it is applied as its own product (1D-LTE, 1D-NLTE and 3D-NLTE are separate rows). Every value carries a full uncertainty budget: fit, line strengths, microturbulence, continuum, fit window, model atmosphere, telluric residual, and the spread between spectra, each measured by refitting with that one input changed. The headline at the top is the Asplund-grade product: a published line set, the most complete treatment, then the most lines.

Excluded lines

These lines are left out of the Sun's measurement. They stay in the line lists: a cooler or more evolved star may measure them well. Blended lines are not excluded -- the spectrum synthesis models the blend. 59 lines.

  • Abundance outlier: disagrees with the other lines well beyond its error, and no solar analysis in the literature uses it.
  • Not measurable: the line falls in a data gap or a saturated telluric band.
  • Saturated: on the flat part of the curve of growth, so the line barely responds to the abundance (reduced width log W/λ above -4.9).

Solar silicon context

Silicon is traced by Si I lines from the blue to the H band and by the single Si II 6371 Å line. The optical lines are Asplund et al. 2021's set (Amarsi & Asplund 2017) with the gf the authors used; the infrared lines are the published sets of Deshmukh et al. 2022 and Elgueta et al. 2026 on Pehlivan Rhodin et al. 2024 oscillator strengths. Each set, spectrum and treatment remains a separate product.
